plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Rolling rows of silvery-green shrubs erupt into waves of violet-blue flower spikes. The air hums with bees and carries a sweet, herbal perfume. Peak bloom turns the countryside into a purple patchwork.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June to early August, with peak bloom in mid-July
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. Romans scented their baths with lavender.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: Dinner-plate-sized blossoms rise above the water on tall stalks, over big round leaves that bead water like quicksilver. Each bloom opens in the morning and closes at night, and lasts about three days.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, around June to July and often later
plants.location: Warm-temperate and tropical Asia, in ponds and lakes across China and Japan
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a microscopic, wax-coated surface that makes water roll off and carry dirt away. This 'lotus effect' has inspired self-cleaning paints and fabrics.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: Daisy-like blooms with drooping rosy-purple petals surround a spiky, copper-orange central cone. Butterflies and goldfinches crowd the flowers across sunny prairies and garden borders.
plants.bloomingSeason: June to September, sometimes reblooming in fall
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, in prairies and open woodlands and in gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Greek 'echinos', meaning hedgehog. It refers to the prickly central cone. Goldfinches often eat the seeds from the spent seed heads in late summer.
